key_insight: Confident but incorrect LLM teaching induced users to adopt falsehoods with high confidence while their trust in the assistant barely changed.
engineering_relevance: Learning interfaces should make reliability visible claim by claim and evaluate human deference alongside model sycophancy.
method: Within-subjects study: 32 participants learned up to five science topics using GPT-5-mini assistants.
Assistant briefings contained 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% plausible falsehoods, all delivered confidently.
Surprise quizzes, answer-confidence ratings, transcript coding, and trust ratings measured learning and deference.
evidence_signal: Across 104 quizzes and 1,040 answers, scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10; confidence discrimination for correctness fell from AUROC 0.70 to chance.
watch_item: The small sample and single underlying model limit generalization beyond this controlled science-learning setting.
paper_title: Who Is Sycophantic to Whom? Confident LLMs, Human Deference, and the Collapse of Trust Calibration
